files.text: # Wargamon A browser RPG set in a fictional modern Indonesia. The runnable game is in `web/` and uses stable numeric IDs for species, trainers, maps, and saves. Do not renumber these IDs: existing browser saves depend on them. ## Run and check ```sh npm run dev # local server, including permanent editor saves # open http://localhost:8000 npm install # once: Prettier for formatting, Sharp for one art test npm test # runs every suite and lists all failures npm run build:generated # after any edit under web/, tests/ or scripts/ npm run format # Prettier over web/, tests/ and scripts/ npm run preview:map 7 # draw region 7 with its walkable ground; also ?debug → Area jalan in the game python3 scripts/audit-assets.py python3 scripts/profile-assets.py ``` For collision-free layout checks, open `http://localhost:8000/?debug`, expand **DEBUG**, and enable **Semua area bisa dijalani** (English: **Walk everywhere**). It allows walking and click navigation across all terrain and residents in the current world, including interiors. Map bounds and chapter connectors still apply. The setting lasts for the browser tab's session; turning it off restores collision and returns the player to valid ground if needed. `npm run build:generated` rewrites the floor data (`web/js/data/floors.js`) and three generated files: `web/i18n/messages.js` (from the catalogs), `web/service-worker.js` (the service worker's file lists) and `web/source-manifest.json`. `npm test` fails when any of them is stale or when a file is not formatted. No npm installation or bundling is required for play; a static server also works (`python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory web`). Permanent editor saves use `npm run dev` (or `python3 scripts/dev-server.py`) and require Node.js plus the existing Sharp development dependency (`npm install` once). `scripts/build-portraits.py` uses Pillow, NumPy, and SciPy when creature source art changes; `scripts/normalize-raster.cjs` uses Sharp when importing a legacy PNG. For art work, install `requirements-art.txt` with pip and run `npm install` once for Sharp; the game itself needs neither. Do not run either conversion script as part of normal page loading. ## Portrait contract - `art(id)` in `web/js/engine/game.js` is the only creature portrait renderer. It emits one `` with the species name as alt text. A missing file remains empty rather than showing a different species. - `web/js/data/creature-portrait-data.js` maps each stable species ID to `web/img/creatures/NNN-name.webp`. Every portrait is 512 × 512 with transparency. New species need one new entry at the end; evolutions use their own stable IDs and files. - `web/js/engine/roster.js` is the only species-to-follower-sheet mapping. Follower atlases are fetched when that species becomes active. Species 70–79 currently show their exact portrait in the world until dedicated directional follower sheets are drawn; do not substitute a different species. - `art/portrait-sources.json` records the editable input sheet or individual image, crop, and matte for each portrait. Run `python3 scripts/build-portraits.py` after editing source art, inspect a contact sheet, and run the asset audit before publishing. - Older sheets in `web/source-art/` remain as source inputs only. The game never requests them and the service worker does not cache them. Game runtime raster assets use WebP, including item icons and the hero sheet. - Item icons use the explicit `ITEM_ART` catalog in `web/js/ui/items.js`. Add one named WebP and a catalog entry for each new item; the asset audit and interface test verify the referenced file. Animation atlases remain sheets because each file carries multiple directional frames. ## Current code layout The code predates a module system: every file is a classic script sharing one global scope, and `web/index.html` declares the load order. Each function has exactly one definition (`tests/single-definition.cjs` enforces it), so to change behaviour, edit the function where it is defined. Nothing is wrapped or reassigned by a later file. ``` web/ index.html the game page; lists every script in load order source.html source download page service-worker.js generated offline cache css/style.css the only stylesheet i18n/ translation: core.js, locales.js, id.json, en.json, messages.js (generated) js/data/ tables with stable IDs js/engine/ state, world, drawing, battle rules, input, loading js/ui/ dialogs, bag, shops, services, saves, Wargadex js/story/ one file per story area or feature img/maps/exterior/ outdoor maps, numbered chapter-map img/maps/interior/ room and arena backgrounds img/characters/ player, trainers, townspeople img/followers/ walking sheets for the lead creature img/creatures/ one portrait per species img/items/ item icons source-art/ editable art inputs; never loaded by the game ``` | Files | What they own | | --- | --- | | `js/data/*.js` | One literal table per file: `elements.js`, `species.js`, `moves.js`, `trainers.js`, `regions.js`, `places.js` (places and rooms). To change a creature, move or place, edit its entry. | | `js/engine/game.js` | Core state, `fresh()`, `normalise()`, `migrateSave()`, saving, the key handler. | | `i18n/core.js`, `i18n/messages.js`, `i18n/locales.js` | Catalog lookup, the generated catalog, and translation of rendered text. | | `js/engine/world.js` | Activity points, rooms, travel, floors and collision, walking, using a point. | | `js/engine/render.js` | The frame loop and everything painted on the map canvas. | | `js/engine/progress.js` | What is unlocked, what may be challenged, the next objective. | | `js/engine/battle.js` | Conditions, moves, turns, capture, the battle screen. | | `js/engine/roster.js`, `sprites.js` | Follower sheets; character and facade sprites. | | `js/engine/controls.js` | Delegated click handlers and pointer input. | | `js/data/places.js`, `js/data/floors.js` | Authored map points and generated walkable floors from `art/floors.json`. | | `js/data/map-geometry.js` | Facing edges of the 15 main maps, their calculated world positions and their touching map edges. | | `js/engine/soundscape.js`, `loading.js` | Audio; image loading and the loading overlay. | | `js/engine/boot.js` | Runs last: migrates the save, wires the toolbar, shows the first screen. | | `js/ui/*.js` | Dialogs and side panels, bag and shops, food/clinic/storage/tutor, civic decisions, save slots and backups, the Dex, the minimarket. | | `js/story/*.js` | Chapters, expansions, the reservoir, the League, the districts, route trainers, the futsal penalty game. | Image names in code are paths from `web/`, for example `img/maps/exterior/1-1.webp`. Main maps connect through opposite painted edges. `WORLD_CONNECTIONS` chooses the outgoing side; the next map's `back` point aligns with the current map's `next` point on the perpendicular axis. Facing edges touch directly, with no filler strip. All 15 outdoor maps use separate native 1536 × 1024 images and one complete WebP each; no split panoramas or shared paintings. Service buildings are drawn into the map artwork. Follow `art/MAP-ART-STANDARD.md` and record generations in `art/independent-map-generation.json`. Walkability comes from the traced painting: a connection must never override a building, tree or water cell. When replacing a map, trace the finished art and check every activity and both directions of travel. Old outdoor saves keep their local position when usable and otherwise move to the nearest connected floor. `web/css/style.css` is the only stylesheet. Rules near the end of the file are there because they must win over earlier rules for the same elements; keep them last. The few remaining `!important` flags override inline styles set by scripts or the `.hidden` utility. - `web/i18n/id.json` and `en.json` are the keyed catalogs; every translated string lives there. Game code writes Indonesian, and `locales.js` finds the English by looking the rendered Indonesian up in the catalog. That means editing Indonesian wording in a script without editing `id.json` silently loses its translation: `tests/i18n-drift.cjs` fails when a catalog entry no longer appears in the source. Entries it cannot check (text assembled at run time) are listed in `tests/i18n-unverified.json`; regenerate with `node tests/i18n-drift.cjs --write` only after checking them by hand. Avoid adding a new language branch inside gameplay code. - `web/js/ui/save-transfer.js` validates versioned portable save files before replacement; the browser autosave key remains `wargamon-v2` and manual slots remain `wargamon-slots`. - `web/js/engine/soundscape.js` owns the music and effects settings; `game.js` only provides a no-op `beep` hook until that module loads. The Menu audio screen is the sole audio control. - `tests/*.cjs` exercise logic in a Node VM. `tests/harness.cjs` reads the script order from `web/index.html`; `setup(storage)` loads every script of the shipped page, so tests exercise the game players get. `tests/full-page.cjs` loads it in both languages. `tests/starter-alpha.cjs` needs `npm install` for Sharp. They cannot replace a browser playthrough, especially for map art, mobile layout, and touch input. - `scripts/audit-assets.py` checks every literal image/audio reference and decodes the shipped rasters. `scripts/update-source-manifest.py` keeps the downloadable source package in sync. - `scripts/profile-assets.py` enforces compressed art and per-file decoded size budgets. Browser portraits use native lazy loading, and only the active follower sheet is requested. The report's all-decoded total is a worst case, not observed device memory. - The service worker (`web/service-worker.js`, generated) fetches the page, scripts and stylesheet from the network first and keeps an all-or-nothing copy for offline play; art is cached on first use and the rest is fetched in the background after the first frame. `scripts/build-offline-cache.py` writes the worker and both lists. - `web/js/engine/loading.js` gives the current map priority, creates a missing map image request, and replaces a failed request when the player taps **Coba lagi**. Optional follower atlases stay unloaded until needed. - The current map also prepares its wild portraits, trainer lineups, linked interior art, and shared item icons. Neighbor maps warm in the background. A fight opens immediately when its prepared portraits are ready; a loading dialog appears only if a required image is still downloading or failed. - The first four map images occupy a fixed 2 × 2 grid: Padang Ojek / Hutan Pinggir Kota above Sukamaju / Gang Senggol. All four floors follow their current paintings: roads, paved alleys, stairs, bridges and clear meadow are walkable; water, roofs, parked bikes and dense planting are blocked. Padang joins Hutan on the dirt road at local y=530. Hutan's southern border contains houses and vegetation, so its route into Gang uses Padang and Sukamaju's painted roads. Residents stand beside usable approaches, and old saves on newly blocked ground recover onto connected floor in their own map. Sukamaju's manually saved grid is preserved. `web/js/story/districts.js` draws Gang without mirroring or an extra connecting road. Pasar Subuh remains a room reached from Pasar Malam, and existing Gang choices and saves retain progress. Rebuild the three traced neighbors with `node scripts/build-floors.cjs --only 1,2,gang`. ## Controls and data WASD/arrows or touch controls move. E/Space interacts. M opens the map, T opens team and bag, and G opens Wargadex. The current region and room determine collision, interactions, encounter lists, and battle backdrops. Progress is saved locally; use **Menu → Unduh cadangan simpanan** before switching browser or device. See [RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md) for verified gates and outstanding public release work. Passing tests does not mean the game has completed mobile, accessibility, content, and rights review. In `?debug`, choose **DEBUG → Edit area jalan** to edit any exterior or interior. Opening it inside a building selects that room automatically; the map selector groups **Peta luar** and **Interior**. Green cells are walkable and gray cells are blocked. Choose **Blok kotak** (Rectangle), select **Terhalang** (Blocked) or **Bisa dijalani** (Walkable), then drag between opposite corners to fill the whole block on release. The outline remains after release; **Semua hijau** (All green) or **Semua abu-abu** (All gray) fills every cell of that selected box, regardless of its previous colours. Cells outside the box stay unchanged. **Kuas** (Brush) paints freehand with a 1×1, 3×3, 5×5, 9×9, or 15×15 brush. **Urungkan/Ulangi** undo and redo a whole edit. Each stroke autosaves a browser draft separately from game saves. **Simpan permanen** writes only the selected scene to the codebase, including rooms that initially share a floor with another interior. Click **Simpan permanen** (Save permanently) to write the **selected map** directly to this checkout. The local server stores its grid as `rows` in `art/floors.json`, rebuilds `web/js/data/floors.js`, and refreshes the offline worker and source manifest. These defaults apply to normal play, other browsers, and future floor builds; the artwork is unchanged. Save each edited map this way. **Pulihkan peta ini** restores the current codebase's default, while undoing a permanent save produces a draft that you can save permanently again. Browser drafts still live in `wargamon-floor-edits-v1`; clearing browser data does not remove codebase saves. The server listens only on loopback, accepts only known map grids, rejects stale project revisions, and restores source/generated files if the build fails. The static server and hosted copies cannot write the checkout. Optional export/import is under **Cadangan**, and is not needed for permanent saves. For artwork edits, open **DEBUG → Edit gambar peta** (English: **Edit map image**) or `http://localhost:8000/art-editor.html` using `npm run dev`. Drag a rectangle, describe the change, and click **Prepare selected area**. The editor makes a native-resolution clean crop plus a marked location reference with surrounding context. Download both, upload them to ChatGPT Plus, and use **Copy instructions**. Import ChatGPT's downloaded result and build the protected preview. The generated context is discarded outside your chosen rectangle; a 32-pixel map border stays locked. Include the whole object, its shadow and some surrounding ground. Larger returned crops are reduced proportionally; different aspect ratios are rejected instead of stretched. Boundary lighting is matched inside the box with Poisson blending, retaining the imported texture and eliminating the former hard paste and 8-pixel strip of the old object. The whole map is never resized. **Save permanently** writes a lossless WebP only after decoding it and verifying **zero changed pixels outside the rectangle**. This guarantee concerns decoded pixels; the encoded file bytes change. The Before/After close-up exposes local seams, and a warning appears when ChatGPT redraws the surrounding context. Check the close-up and its edges before enabling Save. Boundary matching cannot guarantee correct geometry or restore details that the generator redrew. Old hard-paste previews must be rebuilt before saving. The original image, context, returned result and session data remain under `.map-art-edits//`, ignored by Git and excluded from the game's source download. **Previous edits** resumes a session; **Undo this permanent save** restores the original bytes if no newer artwork has replaced them. For chapter crops still matching their source atlas, the corresponding source quadrant is updated too, with every pixel outside the chosen rectangle verified and a source backup retained. Other map images, grid coordinates, connectors and walking areas remain unchanged. Edit walking areas separately when changing obstacles. ChatGPT Plus uses this manual image round trip: the current Sign in with ChatGPT preview does not support the image-generation tool. No API key or JSON export/import is needed. Exterior maps use `chapter-map.webp` in story order: | Chapter | Exterior files in order | | --- | --- | | 1 | `1-1` Sukamaju, `1-2` Padang Ojek, `1-3` Gang Senggol, `1-4` Hutan Pinggir Kota | | 2 | `2-1` Terminal Rame, `2-2` Kota Beton, `2-3` Festival Arus, `2-4` Pasar Malam; `2-5` Pasar Subuh side area | | 3 | `3-1` Pesisir Suaka, `3-2` Kampung Bengkel, `3-3` Taman Waduk, `3-4` Stasiun Sela | | 4 | `4-1` Puncak Sinyal, `4-2` Jalur Kaldera, `4-3` Observatorium Sunyi, `4-4` Liga Nusantara | Interiors keep descriptive names; shared room sheets serve multiple rooms. Historical art archives retain their original filenames.

# Wargamon public release worklist

This is an acceptance list, not a claim that the game is finished. Complete and verify each section before marking it done. Use it to plan and verify release work.

## 1. Save safety and test gate

- [x] Run the complete current automated suite and repair stale assertions.
- [x] Add versioned JSON export of autosave and all ten manual slots.
- [x] Validate a backup before replacing any browser data; show a restore review screen.
- [x] Reject imported saves with markup in text fields, unknown conditions or held items, or out-of-range IDs.
- [x] Test round trip, corrupt/unsupported data, and storage failure rollback.
- [ ] Test backup and restore across two real browsers/devices, including a long late-game save.

## 2. Loading, assets, and performance

- [x] Give all 80 creature portraits one named transparent WebP file and one runtime renderer.
- [x] Convert shipped PNG assets to WebP and remove runtime portrait crops and arbitrary placeholders.
- [ ] Visually review every creature and NPC against a single art guide; repair inconsistent silhouettes, palettes, and cutouts.
- [x] Consolidate function override chains into owned modules: each function has one definition, enforced by `tests/single-definition.cjs`; the README lists what each file owns.

- [ ] Measure first playable time on a typical mobile connection and handset.
- [ ] Load essential map and current team first; reveal optional art only after it is ready.
- [ ] Give a real recovery path for missing images and failed loads; never show unrelated temporary sprites.
- [x] Keep the offline copy consistent: page, scripts and stylesheet are cached together or not at all and refreshed from the network; source art is not cached.
- [x] Fetch follower atlases only for the active species, and show that species' own portrait for forms without follower poses.
- [x] Wait for the current map, visible NPC cuts, active follower cut, and team portraits before hiding the startup overlay; retry failed visible image requests.
- [x] Include adjacent regions visible in the camera, wait for image decode and the first successful frame, and load every trainer lineup portrait before opening its introduction. Retry a failed portrait without substituting another species.
- [x] Give follower atlases one numbered naming convention and map those sheets to stable species IDs in `art/follower-atlases.json`.
- [x] Start an unregistered current-map request and allow a failed map request to be retried with a fresh image object.
- [x] Replace failed creature portrait requests with a neutral retry tile; retry the original species on tap or keyboard activation.
- [x] Check every literal asset reference and decode each shipped raster file during the release gate.
- [ ] Set a budget for downloaded art, memory, and decoded canvas size; profile repeated travel.
- [x] Enforce compressed art and individual decoded-image budgets; defer offscreen creature portraits and inactive follower sheets.

## 3. World and collision

- [ ] Audit all 15 regions and 24 interiors at visible obstacle edges, paths, doors, buses, water, and map transitions.
- [x] Test every activity point against authored walkable geometry and routes in all 15 regions, all 24 interiors, and all 14 travel links; move Bu Lasmi off the clinic facade. The two optional district routes have their own checks.
- [x] Match the paved upper approach at Kaldera, Observatorium, and Liga to authored walkable rectangles; keep lava, buildings, fountain, and boundary props solid, with targeted assertions.
- [ ] Ensure service buildings and entrance markers agree with the art and text.

## 4. Mobile UI and gameplay clarity

- [ ] Test small phone portrait, landscape, tablet, and desktop for clipping, touch selection, and dialog reachability.
- [x] Open directly into the map viewport; move objective, journal, habitat, and places behind Menu > Wilayah; size battle moves as a four-card grid without the old half-height scroller.
- [x] Gate wild fights on decoded opponent/team portraits, decode the current region’s wild roster before revealing its map, mark the exact search point with a grass clump, and replace split-sphere catch icons with an original woven case.
- [ ] Align battle cards, Tempo display, action buttons, team storage, shops, Dex, and tutor screens.
- [ ] Explain combat costs, status, growth, and inventory actions at the point of use.
- [ ] Verify both Indonesian and English across the story and every interactive screen. A scan of the source and of the scripted playthroughs finds no sentence left in Indonesian in English mode; place and character names stay Indonesian on purpose. Story dialogue still needs a read-through by a person.
- [x] Keep every translated string in the catalogs and fail the suite when a catalog entry stops matching the Indonesian source.
- [x] Translate previously missed bag, Wargadex, travel, audio, and trainer labels through the locale catalog; test them in English.
- [x] Offer the old exploration panels as an optional saved setting, with a direct Places shortcut on the play screen.
- [x] Prepare map-adjacent interior and encounter art before the player opens a room or fight; keep the wait dialog for genuinely unfinished or failed downloads.
- [x] Add two optional Indonesian districts with saved civic choices and distinct map art; replace the red-cap player sheet with a transparent local traveler.

## 5. Content and world consistency

- [ ] Complete late-game interiors, NPC artwork, shops, map labels, habitat cues, and story consequences.
- [x] Preserve authored late-game clinic names at entrances and match shop titles to the actual Kaldera, research, and outdoor locations; remove stale clinic prices and development wording from chapter markers.
- [x] Show each terminal stamp and the travel-card capsule reward once; on later visits give a contextual reminder in both languages, including migrated saves that already have the card.
- [ ] Check species silhouettes, evolutionary changes, type spread, encounter distribution, legendary battles, and enemy AI.
- [ ] Replace direct names, marks, and embedded brand imagery that should not ship publicly; review generated art provenance.
- [x] Keep evolution portraits adjacent by Wargadex display number while preserving internal save IDs; replace three near-duplicate adult portraits.
- [x] Replace Cirenggulung's close adult portrait with a distinct guardian silhouette and record its editable source.
- [x] Remove real-person reference fields from shipped trainer data, replace the town's baked store mark, and record new art sources.
- [ ] Review music and sound levels, mute persistence, and accessible alternatives.
- [x] Remove the retired header sound toggle; make zero volume silent, apply music slider changes immediately, and test saved mute and volume preferences.

## 6. Release gate

- [ ] Run full automated suite, scripted save migration, accessibility checks, and manual playthrough.
- [ ] Verify a fresh game and a representative old save on desktop and mobile.
- [ ] Recheck public content, policy pages, player support, credits, and downloadable source.
- [x] Correct the source page's region count and test the downloadable source manifest and ZIP contents.
- [ ] Publish the release candidate and address bugs found by external testers.

The following generation rules apply to future generated maps; the user-supplied quartet above is an explicit exception.

**One generated image = one complete map.** Each map gets its own full-resolution generation. A larger scene containing several maps must never be divided into map assets. Cropped exports of those scenes do not satisfy this rule either.

## 1. Resolution and framing

| Property | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Map artwork | 1536 × 1024 native pixels, landscape, exactly 3:2 |
| Game coordinates | 960 × 640 world units, unchanged map proportions |
| Camera | Consistent existing 600 × 400 world-unit view |
| Generation | Entire single map fills the image; no border, reference frame, collage or extra neighboring map |
| Detail | Native fine detail, checked in the game; enlarged low-resolution artwork is rejected |
| Runtime asset | One independent WebP background per map, retaining 1536 × 1024 |

1536 × 1024 is the baseline, not a claim that dimensions alone guarantee sharpness. At the existing 600 × 400 camera zoom, a map of this size supplies a 960 × 640 source section. The canvas backing dimensions follow the actual displayed size and device pixel ratio. Its old fixed backing size must not reintroduce blur on wide or Retina screens.

Large browser windows enlarge the canvas further. Review both a normal Chrome window and the user's wide-window view. Do not change game zoom to disguise poor artwork. If a genuinely native 1536 × 1024 pilot still lacks detail, revise this baseline before regenerating the remaining maps.

The image tool request must specify these dimensions, but the returned file must also be measured. A prompt is not proof of resolution. Reject undersized or wrong-aspect results; do not stretch, pad, crop or upscale them to pass. A larger native 3:2 single-map result can be reduced uniformly once for export, only if its detail survives visual inspection.

## 2. Drawing style and object scale

- Use the same overhead, slightly oblique RPG view across all maps. No isometric angle changes or closer camera framing between maps.
- Keep clean, fine pixel detail: separate roof tiles, readable window edges, defined leaves, stones and paving. Reject soft painting, smeared foliage, blurry edges and large blocky pixel clusters.
- Use a fixed reference set: an accepted standalone map for detail and perspective, plus the actual player sprite for scale. The existing 1536 × 1024 Pasar Malam image is a candidate detail reference; it is not automatically approved as the master style.
- Match door, tree, vehicle and building scale to the player and adjoining map. Day/night palettes can differ intentionally; apparent pixel size and object scale must remain consistent.
- Draw service buildings, including kantin and puskesmas, into the complete map artwork. Their architecture, shadows and paving must belong to the same scene.
- Keep dynamic people, Wargamon, interaction labels and UI out of the background. Avoid generated long-form lettering. Any necessary short building sign must be legible in the real game.

The first accepted standalone Sukamaju regeneration becomes the reference for subsequent maps. Freeze its camera, detail density, lighting conventions and scale before continuing.

## 3. Connections between independent maps

**Fixed world grid:** every outdoor map owns exactly one 960 × 640 cell. Its origin is `(column × 960, row × 640)`, with integer column and row values. No two maps can occupy the same cell. North/south neighbors have identical horizontal bounds; east/west neighbors have identical vertical bounds. A road or entrance must never shift the map origin. `buildWorldGrid` rejects duplicate cells, contradictory directions and disconnected maps, and shared entrance centers are checked before the game starts.

The camera follows world position continuously, independently of the player's current map. A neighboring map is visible before crossing; a region change cannot hide, reveal or recenter it. The view stays within the union of painted grid cells so empty diagonal cells do not appear as rectangular grass cutouts. Direct neighboring paintings start loading with the active map before its first frame. Camera zoom and native image resolution stay fixed.

Prepare a paired edge specification before generating either map:

| Record | Required information |
| --- | --- |
| Direction | North/south or east/west pair |
| Position | Same crossing center on the facing edges, in world coordinates |
| Corridor | Matching usable width, road edges and clear approach |
| Ground | Matching dirt/asphalt/paving, color, texture scale and elevation |
| Surroundings | Compatible grass, shadows and vegetation; complete nearby buildings |

Example: Sukamaju north edge at x=480 connects to Padang Ojek south edge at x=480. An agreed 80-world-unit corridor is 128 native pixels wide at the required resolution. The same center and width must be used by the image layout, collision mask and transition logic.

Generate **each map separately**, using the adjacent map's edge as a reference. The reference may guide the generation; it must not become part of a multi-map output. Edge specifications describe the full artwork, not a road patch pasted afterward.

Keep complete buildings, roof silhouettes and prominent trees inside their map boundaries. Carry the crossing through clear ground, without cutting a building or canopy in half. Roads may bend naturally within a map, but crossing the boundary must not impose a sideways detour or teleport the player to a different road.

Blend environment changes through the approach terrain inside each map. Reject straight texture seams, sudden road-width changes, mismatched curb heights and roads advertising nonexistent exits. Remove obsolete Sukamaju/Jalur Ojek transition signs.

The shared-scene renderer and artificial 40-unit joining gaps have been removed. Use contiguous facing edges and matching world positions. Each new image must own only its own map extent; never paint it over a neighboring map or insert a makeshift joining strip.

## 4. Walkable ground must match the artwork

Before generation, record doors, entrances, quest locations, roads and solid object footprints on the 960 × 640 layout. After generation, verify their actual positions and trace the finished artwork.

- Open grass and visible public paths are walkable unless an explicit visible obstacle blocks them.
- Water, buildings, walls, tree-covered ground, parked buses and planted beds remain solid.
- Every usable door and advertised exit has a clear reachable approach.
- Do not widen collision corridors through visible obstacles to compensate for an incorrect image. Regenerate an incorrect layout.
- Check walking and click-to-walk in both directions across every changed connection, including progression locks and return journeys.

## 5. Acceptance and export

A map is ready only after all of these checks:

1. **File:** verify actual native dimensions, aspect ratio and one-map provenance. A split scene fails even if its export has the right filename or dimensions.
2. **Artwork:** inspect the entire source and detail areas at native size: roofs, doors, trees, road edges and signage. No clipped objects, patch seams or blurred detail.
3. **Game:** inspect normal and wide-window Chrome views with the player visible. Compare detail and object scale against the accepted reference. A thumbnail is insufficient.
4. **Neighbor:** walk across the seam in both directions. Verify matching ground, corridor width, camera continuity and position, without artificial rerouting.
5. **Collision:** verify open grass, doors and paths; also deliberately attempt to walk into trees, walls, water, buses and buildings.
6. **Export:** compare compressed WebP against the native source at game zoom. Retain dimensions; do not reduce resolution to meet a file-size budget. Prefer lossless or visually verified compression.
7. **Release:** run affected gameplay checks and asset audits. Passing those checks does not replace visual approval.

Keep the accepted native source and generation record outside the shipped game bundle. Retain rejected generation candidates and their prompt records when requested by the user; that retention preference applies to the current map work. Existing size limits must be rechecked during migration; removing duplicate shared paintings should come before sacrificing detail. Each 1536 × 1024 RGBA image decodes to 6 MiB, within the current 7 MiB per-image guard.

# Wargamon art contract

The shipped portraits are now one file per species with identical format and placement. This does not itself guarantee identical drawing style. Use this guide when editing or adding art; review the result beside its neighbors before release.

## Portrait

- Original, recognizable Indonesian everyday subject mixed with a creature. Readable silhouette at 48 px, no words, logo, scenery, UI, or ground plate baked into the creature.
- Three-quarter front view facing toward the opponent when shown on the player's side. Keep body and detached effects within the central 480 px of a 512 × 512 transparent canvas; no accidental crop at horns, tail, or feet.
- Bold dark outline with restrained variation; saturated but limited colors; bright upper-left light; two to three stepped shadows. Pixel edges should remain legible at small sizes. Avoid photorealistic or soft airbrushed surfaces.
- Base forms should look small and approachable. Evolutions should change silhouette and role substantially, with a larger build, new functional parts, and a distinct stance. A recolor or a copied body with added horns is insufficient.
- No opaque backdrop, checkerboard, unrelated prop, duplicate creature, brand mark, or text. Preserve alpha around the silhouette.

## Files and pipeline

1. Keep editable input in `web/source-art/` with a descriptive WebP name. Add a measured entry to `art/portrait-sources.json` with the stable internal species ID. `art/dex-order.json` records the separate display order.
2. Run `python3 scripts/build-portraits.py` to make `web/img/creatures/NNN-name.webp` and regenerate its runtime path. The filename number is the Wargadex number, so evolution families stay adjacent; saves still use the stable ID. Inspect the creature at 48, 96, and 160 px and compare it with nearby species and its evolution.
3. Run `npm test` and `python3 scripts/audit-assets.py`. Confirm the portrait is transparent, is the intended species, and is used in battle, Wargadex, team, tutor, storage, and shops where applicable.
4. Add overworld follower poses separately. Portraits and follower sheets share species design, but followers are not substituted for portraits.

The source manifest preserves old input art for reproducible builds; only `web/img/creatures/` is the runtime portrait source.

"""Build one 512px transparent WebP per species from the editable source art.

The source manifest records measured crops and the matte used for each batch.
Rebuilds are deterministic; browser code never crops or substitutes a portrait.
"""
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from scipy import ndimage

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
DIST = ROOT / 'web'
OUT = DIST / 'img' / 'creatures'
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
SPECIES = json.loads((ROOT / 'art' / 'portrait-sources.json').read_text())['species']
DEX_ORDER = json.loads((ROOT / 'art' / 'dex-order.json').read_text())['display_order']
assert len(DEX_ORDER) == len(SPECIES) and sorted(DEX_ORDER) == list(range(len(SPECIES)))
for display_number, internal_id in enumerate(DEX_ORDER, 1):
    spec = SPECIES[internal_id]
    assert spec['id'] == internal_id and spec['slug'].startswith(f'{display_number:03d}-'), spec
FOUR = ndimage.generate_binary_structure(2, 1)


def remove_connected_background(data, candidates, mode):
    labels, count = ndimage.label(candidates, FOUR)
    if not count:
        return
    edge = np.unique(np.concatenate((labels[0], labels[-1], labels[:, 0], labels[:, -1])))
    discard = np.zeros(count + 1, dtype=bool)
    discard[edge] = True
    discard[0] = False
    if mode == 'generated':
        red = data[:, :, 0]
        for component in range(1, count + 1):
            if discard[component]:
                continue
            region = labels == component
            if region.sum() > 32 and red[region].min() < 200 and red[region].max() > 225:
                discard[component] = True
    data[:, :, 3][discard[labels]] = 0


def isolate(image, matte):
    data = np.array(image.convert('RGBA'))
    if matte == 'generated':
        rgb = data[:, :, :3].astype(np.int16)
        neutral = (data[:, :, 3] < 20) | ((rgb.min(axis=2) >= 125) & (np.ptp(rgb, axis=2) <= 22))
        remove_connected_background(data, neutral, 'generated')
    if matte in ('cream', 'generated', 'actor'):
        rgb = data[:, :, :3].astype(np.int16)
        if matte == 'actor':
            neutral = (data[:, :, 3] < 20) | ((rgb.min(axis=2) > 170) & (np.ptp(rgb, axis=2) < 15))
        else:
            neutral = (data[:, :, 3] < 20) | ((rgb[:, :, 0] > 239) & (rgb[:, :, 1] > 233) & (rgb[:, :, 2] > 205))
        remove_connected_background(data, neutral, matte)
    if matte in ('cream', 'generated'):
        components, count = ndimage.label(data[:, :, 3] >= 20, FOUR)
        sizes = np.bincount(components.ravel())
        largest = max(sizes[1:], default=0)
        if largest:
            remove = np.zeros(count + 1, dtype=bool)
            remove[1:] = sizes[1:] < largest * .012
            data[:, :, 3][remove[components]] = 0
    return Image.fromarray(data, 'RGBA')


def crop(spec):
    image = Image.open(DIST / spec['source']).convert('RGBA')
    if 'rect' in spec:
        x, y, w, h = spec['rect']
        if spec.get('fractional'):
            x, y, w, h = round(x * image.width / 4), 0, round(image.width / 4), image.height
        else:
            base_w, base_h = spec['basis']
            x, y = round(x * image.width / base_w), round(y * image.height / base_h)
            w, h = round(w * image.width / base_w), round(h * image.height / base_h)
        image = image.crop((x, y, x + w, y + h))
    return image


for spec in SPECIES:
    if os.environ.get('PORTRAIT_ONLY') and spec['slug'] != os.environ['PORTRAIT_ONLY']:
        continue
    art = isolate(crop(spec), spec['matte'])
    box = art.getchannel('A').point(lambda alpha: 255 if alpha >= 20 else 0).getbbox()
    if box is None:
        raise SystemExit(f"{spec['name']}: extraction produced no artwork")
    art = art.crop(box)
    scale = 480 / max(art.size)
    size = (max(1, round(art.width * scale)), max(1, round(art.height * scale)))
    art = art.resize(size, Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
    canvas = Image.new('RGBA', (512, 512))
    canvas.alpha_composite(art, ((512 - size[0]) // 2, (512 - size[1]) // 2))
    
    destination = OUT / f"{spec['slug']}.webp"
    temporary = OUT / f".{spec['slug']}.tmp.webp"
    for attempt, method in enumerate((4, 0, 0)):
        canvas.save(temporary, 'WEBP', quality=90, method=method)
        try:
            with Image.open(temporary) as check:
                check.verify()
            with temporary.open('rb+') as stable:
                os.fsync(stable.fileno())
            temporary.replace(destination)
            break
        except Exception:
            if attempt == 2:
                raise SystemExit(f"{spec['name']}: WebP encoder failed after three attempts")
    temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
if not os.environ.get('PORTRAIT_ONLY'):
    for spec in SPECIES:
        with Image.open(OUT / f"{spec['slug']}.webp") as check:
            if check.size != (512, 512):
                raise SystemExit(f"{spec['name']}: unexpected portrait dimensions")
            check.verify()
    entries = [f"img/creatures/{spec['slug']}.webp" for spec in SPECIES]
    (DIST / 'js/data/creature-portrait-data.js').write_text('const CREATURE_PORTRAITS=' + json.dumps(entries, ensure_ascii=False) + ';\n')
print(f"Built {1 if os.environ.get('PORTRAIT_ONLY') else len(SPECIES)} individual transparent WebP portraits")

"""Budget the raster art shipped to players (excluding downloadable source art)."""
from pathlib import Path
from PIL import Image

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'web'
groups = {
    # Fifteen independent native 1536 × 1024 map paintings; no duplicate atlases.
    'world, character and item art': ([p for p in (root / 'img').rglob('*.webp') if p.parent.name != 'creatures'], 24 * 1024**2),
    'creature portraits': (list((root / 'img' / 'creatures').glob('*.webp')), 7 * 1024**2),
}
largest_file_budget = 800 * 1024
decoded_file_budget = 7 * 1024**2
errors = []

for label, (files, compressed_budget) in groups.items():
    compressed = sum(file.stat().st_size for file in files)
    decoded = 0
    for file in files:
        with Image.open(file) as image:
            pixels = image.width * image.height * 4
        decoded += pixels
        if pixels > decoded_file_budget:
            errors.append(f'{file.name}: {pixels / 1024**2:.1f} MiB decoded; limit 7 MiB')
        file_budget = 1280 * 1024 if "maps" in file.relative_to(root).parts and pixels == 1536 * 1024 * 4 else largest_file_budget
        if file.stat().st_size > file_budget:
            errors.append(f'{file.name}: {file.stat().st_size / 1024:.0f} KiB; limit {file_budget / 1024:.0f} KiB')
    if compressed > compressed_budget:
        errors.append(f'{label}: {compressed / 1024**2:.1f} MiB compressed; limit {compressed_budget / 1024**2:.0f} MiB')
    print(f'{label}: {len(files)} files, {compressed / 1024**2:.2f} MiB transfer, '
          f'{decoded / 1024**2:.1f} MiB if all decoded concurrently')

if errors:
    raise SystemExit('\n'.join(errors))
print('PASS raster transfer and per-file decode budgets')

for p in [root / 'README.md', root / 'RELEASE.md', root / 'package.json', root / 'requirements-art.txt', *sorted((root / 'art').glob('*.json')), *sorted((root / 'art').glob('*.md')), *sorted((root / 'tests').glob('*.cjs')), *sorted((root / 'scripts').glob('*.py')), *sorted((root / 'scripts').glob('*.cjs'))]:
    files.append({'path': 'wargamon/' + p.relative_to(root).as_posix(), 'text': p.read_text()})
target = root / 'web/source-manifest.json'
content = json.dumps({'files': files}, ensure_ascii=False)
# --check fails when the committed manifest no longer matches the sources.
if '--check' in sys.argv:
    if not target.is_file() or target.read_text() != content:
        raise SystemExit('web/source-manifest.json is out of date. Run python3 scripts/update-source-manifest.py')
    print(f'Source manifest is current: {len(files)} entries')
else:
    target.write_text(content)
    print(f'Source manifest: {len(files)} entries plus manifest')
